eva: Quick summary from my spike — progressive layerwise decryption + streaming seems promising to reduce peak memory and PCIe bandwidth for large safetensors checkpoints. Key idea: decrypt and materialize layers on demand as the KV cache requests them, but stream encrypted chunks in order.
jia: Nice. Two quick questions: 1) how do we authenticate/authorize per-layer decrypts with KMS without a ton of round trips? 2) fallback behavior if decryption of a mid-layer fails?
omar: For 1) attach a short-lived signed token in the checkpoint header (HMAC over checkpoint id + expire_ts) that our private plane can mint once when the load begins. KMS only used for the master unwrap during onboarding. That token authorizes per-layer unwraps locally. For 2) we retry N times, then mark the shard corrupt and fall back to alternate model variant (quantized copy) per routing policy.
ryan: Operational tradeoff: token-in-header works, but we must ensure revocation for private deployments. For VPC/on-prem, customer KMS policies might require us to call their KMS for per-layer unwraps. So implement two modes: token mode (hosted default) and per-layer KMS mode (enterprise).
eva: Agreed. Also found a useful memory pattern: keep a tiny decrypted page cache per-GPU (4–8 layers), with LRU eviction and zeroing before release. Aim: peak decrypted bytes << full model footprint.
jia: What about prefix/KV cache access patterns? If prompts produce hot prefixes that need lower layers quickly, we may get high churn. Any prefetch heuristics?
omar: We can prefetch the next N contiguous layers when a layer is hot for X requests/s or when cumulative token generation latency goes above threshold. Configurable backoff to avoid overfetch.
ryan: Need a credit-based backpressure from runtime to loader. Runtime issues 'decrypt credits' per worker; loader only decrypts while credits > 0. Prevents IO/decrypt storms during cold startups.
eva: Exactly — I prototyped a token bucket where each token equals one layer decrypt or one contiguous microchunk. Credits refill based on current latency SLO headroom.
warmup-bot: warmup-bot: warmup job started: job_id=wnp-833, model=redwood-m-70b-encrypted, mode=progressive-decrypt, creds_mode=token-header
warmup-bot: warmup-bot: logs:
```
[00:00:01] fetch header -> ok (keys: kt-01, token-expires: 1670000000)
[00:00:03] stream shard chunk 0..8MB -> ok
[00:00:03] decrypt layer 0 -> ok (16MB)
[00:00:04] populate GPU slab -> ok
[00:00:05] prefetch hint: layer 1 hot -> issued 1 decrypt-credit
```
jia: Nice logs. How are we encoding per-layer metadata in the checkpoint? Encrypted IVs, encrypted lengths, per-layer digest?
omar: Header sketch I used: `checkpoint_header = {magic, version, kms_key_id, token_sig, layer_index_count, meta_table_offset}` then separate meta table contains per-layer entries: {offset, enc_len, iv, aad, digest}. Meta table itself can be compressed and signed.
eva: Important: keep meta_table small and unencrypted so runtime can quickly decide on prefetch without KMS. Only the layer payloads stay encrypted. That supports manifestless streaming where loader can decide which byte ranges to request.
ryan: Security note: leaving offsets unencrypted leaks layer sizes and order. Acceptable? For most customers yes, but we should provide an opt-in 'full header encryption' mode for highly sensitive users — at the cost of calling KMS to unlock meta_table first.
jia: Good call. Also think through atomicity: if we decrypt several layers then crash, do we need a wipe-on-boot guarantee? For private deployments with HSM we must document memory zeroing and page guard behavior.
eva: Plan: on eviction we overwrite with zeros on CPU then GPU zero via cuMemset, and persist an audit log entry (in console) for enterprise customers. For hosted we also rotate tokens if we observe suspicious access patterns.
omar: Metrics we should add: per-layer decrypt latency histogram, decrypt-credit utilization, average decrypted-resident-bytes, wasted-decrypts (prefetch but not used), and fallback-rate-to-variant.
ryan: Also track KMS call rate and token mint latency. These inform whether to switch tenants to token-header mode or per-layer KMS.
weston: (quick note) If we implement progressive decrypt, ensure compatibility with cold snapshot restore — ability to hydrate minimal KV cache to start low-latency serving while continuing background decrypts.
eva: Yep. That's the goal — start serving within ~200–300ms by hydrating first-layer embeddings + kvroots, then stream rest.
jia: Ok next steps: 1) formalize header spec and token format, 2) implement credit API in runtime, 3) prototype small prefetch policy and measure wasted-decrypts on real workload. Anyone disagree?
omar: Sounds good. I'll draft header spec and meta_table layout by EOD.
ryan: I'll PR the runtime credit API spike tomorrow.
eva: I'll run experiments to tune token-bucket parameters and prefetch thresholds.
